          INITIAL POST HEARING BRIEF OF INTERVENOR GEORGE NOELKE

COMES NOW George Noelke ('Noelke"), pro se, to submit his initial briefpursuant to SOAH Order
No. 6 inthis case, 59475.

  I.       Introduction
       A. Noelke is directly impacted by proposed route 228 in CCN 59182. Route 228 is the preferred
           route of Applicants in that CCN and was ruled as the recommended route by the ALJ's in the
           PFD. The PFD in 59182 was issued on June 9,2026. Noelke filed his exceptions to the PFD
          prior to any deadline being set. Item 544.
       B. Noelke has timely filed this Initial Brief as required by SOAH Order No. 32, Item 6136.


 II.       Legal Argument
       A. Noelke adds a single legal argument in 59475 and otherwise seeks to preserve his legal
           arguments in 59182 without restating them verbatim here. His additional claim in 59475 is that
          the 839 en masse intervenor dismissals negatively impacted his rights to fully litigate all issues in
          the case. He has already fully argued that position, and incorporates those arguments here. See
           Items 4806, 4932, 5105, 5383 and 5834, SOAH Order No. 29 at page 5. Noelke concurs with the
           Office of the Public Utility Counsel that the quantity of stricken intervenors reflects a need for
          "process improvements" on the front end. 1 See The Office of Public Utility Counsel's Initial Post
         Hearing Brief, Item 6179. Noelke contends that those "process improvements" are transparent
         and already in place. Applicants should be required by SOAH to carry their own water ifthey
         seek to dismiss intervenors by the sanctioning rule. The rules of fairness are in the rule: notice by
         Applicants and an opportunity for a hearing. Any process improvement that fails to follow the
         rule already in place makes it appear that NOAH, as an agency, was just as desperate as
         Applicants to manage the 180 day clock by summarily disposing ofas many of an estimated
         1,800+ interventors as quickly and quietly as possible.
    B. Otherwise, Noelke incorporates here by reference the arguments he raised in 59182. Generally,
         those arguments include that safety issues relating to potential AC interference from paralleling or
         crossing pipelines must be considered as an engineering constraint when selecting the route.
         Applicants lack more than a mere scintilla of evidence (thus less than preponderance) for Route
         228 because they are relying solely on the speculative opinion testimony of a single Oncor
         employee, Corin Cooley, that AC mitigation can be accomplished in 765 kV lines. Secondly,
         Applicants' cost estimates are incorrect because they fail to include the costs ofAC mitigation.
    C. Noelke has filed Exceptions to the PFD in 59182, and those arguments may also be relevant for
         consideration inthe drafting ofthe PFD in 59475. See Item 544 in 59182.
    D. Nothing during the hearing on the merits in 59475 changed his 59182 arguments, and, if
         anything, sharpened their relevancy, The Applicants continue to rely on Ms. Cooley's opinion
         about Applicants' experience in less than 765 kV lines, and no party quantified the cost ofAC
         mitigation.
    E. Noelke Exh 1 for 59475 was admitted, and it establishes two important facts:
         1. Applicants anticipate that they will NOT be paying any pipeline operator/owner for the costs of
         necessary safety improvements for any route in this Application; and,
         2. dll routes in this Application parallel or intersect the Matterhom Express Pipeline. See Noelke
         Exh. 1 at RFI 1-02 and 1-03, Item 5381.
    F.   The Eiger Express Pipeline will parallel the Matterhom in the same easement and will be installed
         and operational before Applicants' 765 kV lines are operational. (Noelke Direct Testimony,
         59182, Item 139.) This means that Applicants' 765 kV line in this case will be crossing 6.2
         billion cubic feet of compressed natural gas each day at potentially multiple locations. Id and see
         Noelke Exh. 1 at RFI 1-04, Item 5381.




1 NOelke notes that OPUC, like any party, might have made its process improvement recommendations on the front
end and in the form of legal argument, as Noelke did before any of the 839 Intervenors were sacrificed.


                                                                                                                 2
 VI. Conclusion

Noelke re-urges his 59182 arguments in his Initial Trial Brief (Item 432), Reply Brief (Item 443) and
Exceptions to the PFD (Item 544). Because every route in 59475 crosses or parallels the Mattehom and
Eiger Pipeline, no route is valid. Moverover, Applicants' cost estimates for every route is invalid for the
reasons stated above. Finally, the en masse dismissal of 839 Intervenors adversely impacted his rights to
fully litigate this case and respond to every issue.
